answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns. Courtship rounds are events only: no ordinary player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview; Round-track events: courtship is only the event.

answers.answer: Hosting order: (1) move servants in Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, then Expended Service to Servants’ Quarters, one space each; unused Available servants stay. (2) Resolve round-track event, then applicable monuments and Servants’ Hall in any order. (3) Choose an activity tile. (4) Invite the exact required gentry. (5) Assign available servants to all required service icons, using permitted substitutions. (6) Resolve all positive favours before negative ones. (7) Optionally buy one improvement. (8) Send every servant used to Expended Service, played gentry to personal discard, and return the activity tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Last player advances the marker.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hosting an activity; Player Reference → Host.

answers.answer: Pass order: all servants directly to Available Service; all gentry in personal discard to hand; round-track event then ongoing effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; then the last player advances the marker. Any servant used for an ongoing effect is expended at turn end. There are no passing activity favours or tile flips. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Passing.

answers.answer: Yes, the activity remains legal because screening was fixed at 6.1 after step 2, and later reputation losses do not invalidate the activity or guests. Service Help moves a servant only from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, not directly from Expended Service. One inconsistency in the scenario: four uses at 3 increments each would lower 6.1 by 12 increments, not to 3.4 under the summary’s increment rules; the stated 3.4 endpoint is unsupported by those quantities.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions; Special Rules & Edge Cases.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; otherwise their order is your choice. At minimum reputation, you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid the loss: negative-reputation guests may be played and losses stop at minimum, but positive favours are resolved first. A money penalty must be fully payable; use positive activity money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money if necessary. If unable to fund it, you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hosting an activity; Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions.

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments and gains £100; repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments and fully refreshes the Market; the special-action refresh is once per turn. No special action is available at minimum reputation. Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions; Player Reference → Costs.

answers.answer: Host Butler’s Room with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service; there is no fee. On first use the room upgrades. Its upgraded option instead recruits one common servant (footman, valet, or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Actions → Servants and hiring; Turn Structure: Butler’s Room has no gentry.

answers.answer: A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman), even when that regular type remains available.
answers.evidence: Actions → Servants and hiring.

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is to purchase Butler’s Pantry; take one from supply immediately into Expended Service. It is not immediately available: ordinarily it moves to Servants’ Quarters at your next service rotation, then to Available Service at your second subsequent rotation. Passing or Refresh Service VP card can make it available earlier; once it is in Quarters, Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can allow earlier use. Another player cannot recruit an underbutler: upgraded Butler’s Room recruits only common servants, and Hire Servant VP cards exclude underbutlers.
answers.evidence: Actions → Servants and hiring; Objectives and VP cards → Hire Servant.

answers.answer: Market price is the market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot be below £100. You may never acquire a duplicate tile you already own. Reputation does not restrict purchasing, so a tile above your reputation may be bought.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on its matching Market tile and another tile is drawn. A Reserve-eligible tile goes straight to Reserve and another is drawn. If filling multiple spaces, sort only the newly drawn tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves its space occupied, so there is no refill.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Refill.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws also go directly there, with the same exception. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve; later PR1 draws go directly there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. A full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Open Reserve and Refresh; Overview.

answers.answer: At each courtship, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. At courtships 1–3, score the current face-up theme category’s tile VP, including negatives; only the face-up hybrid category counts. Highest score gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand. On a top-score tie, each tied player draws one VP card and nobody gets a Fairchild. Everyone discards one secret objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and put them face down on the bottom of the objective deck. After courtships 1–3, open Reserve, fully refresh Market, reveal the next theme to the right of the revealed themes, pass first-player marker anticlockwise, then advance the round marker.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Courtship and seasonal upkeep.

answers.answer: At final courtship, return Fairchilds as usual and score tile VP for all four revealed themes; a category appearing twice counts twice, including negative VP. Highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild. Ties are broken by highest reputation level (wheel position ignored); if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the courtship tie rule. Discard the final objective. Before scoring, players get one final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible; then move the marker to Wedding Bells and score.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Final courtship (round 16).

answers.answer: End-game VP comes from improvement tiles (all printed face-up VP, including negatives and unused tiles), gentry in hand and discard (including family and final Fairchild, excluding dismissed guests), fulfilled objectives, reputation level, servants, wealth, and retained unused VP cards. Reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP. Wealth scores 1 VP per £200, rounded down. Victory ties: player with final Fairchild wins; otherwise highest reputation level wins; if still tied, share victory. Wheel position never breaks final courtship or game ties.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Final VP.

answers.answer: Normally receive five objectives at setup plus two at round 6 (seven total). Discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score; extra objectives add to the retained total without adding a discard. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together, face down to the deck bottom. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles at game end; they need not show upgraded sides.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards; Round-track events: Draw Objectives.

answers.answer: A VP card benefit may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on a later own turn (multiple cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP; a card cannot provide both its benefit and final VP.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded on later uses. Ongoing-only tiles cannot host activities or upgrade. Hybrids start with underlined category showing, flip after every use, and their face-up category counts. Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite host only their front-side activity once, then upgrade into monuments and cannot host again; monument benefits begin on later turns. For courtship and objectives, a hybrid’s currently face-up category is the one counted.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects; Builders’ Market and Reserve.

answers.answer: Monuments give one reputation during the ongoing-effects step on each ordinary hosting or passing turn; none during courtship, and a newly purchased monument first pays on a later turn. Servants’ Hall works in that same step (step 2 when hosting, step 3 when passing): place one available servant on it to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one yourself; that servant cannot also serve the activity and is expended at turn end. Do not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects; Overview.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite uses one casual guest from hand, a footman on the tile, and the guest’s normal service; double all guest favours, positive and negative; it upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite uses one prestige guest from hand, a housekeeper on the tile, and the guest’s normal service; double one chosen favour and resolve others normally; it upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend, requires a butler on the tile and no personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, excluding negative favours from doubling; keep the guest in discard at cleanup, and the tile upgrades into a monument. All have a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: suite activity table and following paragraph.

answers.answer: Choose a random first player. Starting with that player’s left and going clockwise, each player chooses an available base family board. Bonuses: Asquith adds the Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Set each player to reputation level 1, position 1; use the 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters with 1 showing and Max at bottom; do not use 7/8 counters in standard play. Each receives one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; five starting tiles (Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green) with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady family cards. Asquith also gets Dowager Countess. Only Ponsonby starts with money, £300 (apart from Cavendish’s reputation and York’s footman bonus).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2, 3 and 5.

answers.answer: For three players, Servants for Hire gets 3 valets, 3 lady’s maids, 6 footmen and 2 underbutlers. No butlers or housekeepers. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable for this game.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6.

answers.answer: Separate starter guests from the casual deck, shuffle them and deal two to each player’s hand. Shuffle every undealt starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and follow ordinary casual rules, not a separate guest type during play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Actions → Gentry, screening, dismissal and family.

answers.answer: For four players, put five selected double-sided monuments into the bag (one per player plus one). Select at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count toward the five selected monuments.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Fill six different eligible Market spaces: tiles must be PR3 or less (or have no PR), and cannot be Servants’ Hall or a double-sided monument. Set ineligible draws aside and return them to the bag after filling; stack eligible duplicates in a matching space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort the six spaces by ascending printed sorting number, starting at the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately. Reveal the first theme for open courtship; keep revealed themes in order through the game. Put base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild cards face up on Alderley Hall. The first theme is face up, and earlier revealed themes remain in order rather than leaving play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9; Scoring / Victory Conditions → final courtship.

answers.answer: At hosting-turn rotation, the servant in Servants’ Quarters moves to Available Service, while the servant in Expended Service moves to Servants’ Quarters. Any available servant not used remains available.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hosting an activity, step 1.

answers.answer: No. Village Fair resolves before choosing/hosting the activity, so an unupgraded Private Study at that point gives no reward even if upgraded later that turn. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9 only.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table; Improvements and ongoing effects → Private Study.

answers.answer: The round-track event resolves before ongoing tile effects and activity choice on each player’s turn; on space 6 draw two objectives and keep both secret with the others. It is an event on each player’s turn, including a passing player’s turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hosting an activity; Passing; Round-track events table.

answers.answer: Yes. On National Holiday, ignore PR on all tiles and guests when hosting, so lower-reputation players may play higher-PR ones. All other requirements remain, including exact gentry counts and types, service requirements, and other activity conditions.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table; Actions → reputation screening.

answers.answer: On Builders’ Holiday, buy any number from the current Market and/or Reserve within available funds. Complete all purchases before sliding/refilling; use the unchanged market and its existing prices. Do not refresh between purchases with a special action or VP card once a Holiday purchase has occurred. Refill all resulting empty spaces together afterward. Market Purchase VP cards use the same Builders’ Holiday rules.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table; Builders’ Market and Reserve → Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while drawing replacements; keep Reserve unchanged. Refill all six spaces under normal refill rules, then return set-aside tiles to the bag and mix. Those removed tiles cannot reappear in that same refresh.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Refresh.

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment. Move clockwise to gain and anticlockwise to lose; crossing position 5 to 1 raises a level, while crossing 1 to 5 lowers a level. Standard minimum is 1.1 and maximum 7.5 (Max.5); ignore losses beyond minimum. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; take special actions before or during a reputation favour to create space.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions.

answers.answer: Money is public, not secret. Players may not give or receive money from each other. Costs may not exceed holdings; never spend more than you have. The common money supply is unlimited (use proxies if needed).
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions.

answers.answer: Family members cannot fill a ladies-only or casual-guest-only requirement: gentry counts and types must match exactly, with no extras. Family members have no PR and need no personal service, but can fill a family or general gentry requirement as allowed by the printed activity.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hosting an activity, Invite gentry; reputation screening paragraph.

answers.answer: For screening, draw the stated number, choose how many to keep, reveal only kept cards and add them to hand; put rejected cards on the bottom of the guest deck without revealing them. For an ordinary invite, draw from the indicated deck, reveal the guest to everyone and add it to hand.
answers.evidence: Actions → Gentry, screening, dismissal and family.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so with no unwanted guests you need not dismiss. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including a guest drawn earlier in Enjoy Favours. Family cannot be dismissed. Put the dismissed guest on the bottom of its matching guest deck; it is no longer yours, does not return on passing, and does not score for you.
answers.evidence: Actions → Gentry, screening, dismissal and family.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose either screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. The Lady and Heir offer choices; Lord and Dowager give their stated benefits, and Dowager gives both.
answers.evidence: Actions → Gentry, screening, dismissal and family (base family card table).

answers.answer: The Young Lady always draws one casual guest. She gains two reputation only if a male prestige guest attends the same activity: not with a male casual guest, yes with a female prestige guest only if that guest is male (the described female prestige guest does not qualify), and yes with Charles Fairchild because Fairchilds behave as prestige guests and Charles is male.
answers.evidence: Actions → Gentry, screening, dismissal and family; Fairchilds behave as prestige guests.

answers.answer: Charles gives three reputation; he is a prestige guest with no PR and requires a valet. Elizabeth gives both one prestige guest and two reputation; she is a prestige guest with no PR and requires a lady’s maid. Fairchilds behave as prestige guests for play, discard and recovery, not family cards; family dismissal immunity does not apply to them.
answers.evidence: Actions → Gentry, screening, dismissal and family; reputation screening paragraph.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes you lose one reputation. Minimum-reputation protection applies, so a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Actions → Gentry, screening, dismissal and family; Reputation paragraph.

answers.answer: The Barn earns one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile or passing earns none.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Barn.

answers.answer: The Servants’ Quarters tile lets you use one servant from the Servants’ Quarters area each turn in addition to Available Service; its use is separate from ordinary rotation and from Service Help. The servant used through it goes to Expended Service at turn end. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation increments and moves one servant from Quarters to Available Service. Maximum one servant from the tile per turn.
answers.evidence: Actions → Servants and hiring; Reputation, wealth and special actions.

answers.answer: The front-side Private Study requires a butler and two family members; it has no tile favour. After first use it upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile. It is not hosted again: its upgraded side gives £300 and two reputation only on Village Fair rounds (spaces 3 and 9).
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Private Study; Round-track events table.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library requires a butler and two family members and draws one extra objective. Upgraded Main Library requires a butler and three family members and draws one VP card. The extra objective increases the number retained for final scoring; it does not cause an extra courtship discard.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Main Library; Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: The Objective VP card draws two objectives, keeps one and returns the other to the bottom of the objective deck. The retained objective is an additional objective for final scoring.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards → Objective benefit.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available Service and they can be used immediately, including servants from Expended Service. Service Help instead moves only one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service and cannot take directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards → Refresh Service; Reputation, wealth and special actions.

answers.answer: Hire Servant takes one servant from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutler, into Expended Service. It cannot immediately provide service from there (unless subsequently made available by some applicable effect).
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards → Hire Servant.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest returns one gentry card of choice from personal discard to hand; gentry includes family or guests, so a family member may be returned. The card is usable immediately, so the returned family member can attend the activity if its requirements allow.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Invite gentry says gentry includes any family or guest; Objectives and VP cards → Refresh Guest.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets and lady’s maids, excluding butler, housekeeper and underbutler. Ordinary servant VP is 2 VP for every servant of all types and locations. The ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Final VP table.

answers.answer: Upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite count as monuments for the monument objective (3 VP each). Category objectives count a tile in the category currently shown by its face-up side; hybrids count only in their current face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Improvements and ongoing effects.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus any one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus either Main Library or North Library. Objectives require owning the named tiles at game end, not having used them or upgraded them.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: The prestige-guest objective scores 1 VP per prestige guest. The every-three-guests objective scores 1 VP per complete group of three nonfamily guests; an incomplete group scores nothing. A final Fairchild counts as a prestige guest and therefore counts for these objectives if retained.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference.

answers.answer: The reputation objective awards 7 VP for reaching maximum level (level 7), regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective awards 10 VP for at least £1200. Reputation wheel position does not affect ordinary reputation VP (level-based table) or reputation tie resolution (level only).
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Final VP table; courtship and victory tie rules.

answers.answer: West Terrace’s front side requires a butler and three family and invites one prestige guest; the summary does not state its favours, so that part is unsupported. On its upgraded side it also optionally dismisses one to four guests, remains an activity tile, and does not become an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects gives the stated service, attendee, upgrade and dismissal information but does not list favours.

answers.answer: There is no hand or personal discard-pile limit. Gentry in discard still belong to you and score normally; passing returns discard-pile gentry to hand.
answers.evidence: Actions → Gentry, screening, dismissal and family; Passing.

answers.answer: Reserve tiles are public and may be inspected at any time. The summary does not specify whether stacked Reserve tiles are all inspectable/buyable or whether only the top tile may be purchased.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Open Reserve says all Reserve tiles are public and may be inspected at any time; no stack purchase rule stated.

answers.answer: You are not required to host whenever able; each ordinary turn choose to host or pass. If you lack the exact gentry or all required servants for an activity, choose another legal activity or pass; if none is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hosting an activity, Choose activity/Invite gentry/Provide service.

answers.answer: Yes. A passing player may take the free Market refresh benefit, also use the special-action Refresh Market once that turn (if reputation permits), and use Market Refresh VP cards. Only the special-action refresh is limited to once per turn; passing and VP-card refresh methods do not use that allowance.
answers.evidence: Passing; Reputation paragraph; VP-card benefits; Special Rules & Edge Cases.
